One task / One useful finish

What would you like to do?

Choose one useful next step. You do not need to visit every section or finish a course.

  • Write a clearer AI task brief: leave with a plain-text brief and a check you can perform.
  • Check an AI answer: independently verify one important claim and keep what remains uncertain.
  • Make a little room in the week: verify commitments, choose one action, and decide what can wait.
  • Get ready for a first live poker tournament: prepare for arrival and identify venue details to confirm.

Looking for a blank worksheet or calculator? Open Resources. Already know the page or topic? Search for it. Stopping after one useful result is enough.

What you are reading

The labels matter.

Essays explore an idea. Practical guides offer an approach to try. Worked examples and fictional poker hands explain a method; they are not personal case studies. Resource directories point to other people's work, not work I am claiming as my own.

AI assistance is disclosed on the relevant articles. Proposed experiments in Field notes are plans, not completed results.

Follow what interests you, use what helps, and send a thought or correction.
